page: Microsoft Azure E2ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable. The CPU architecture features 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography enabled, while lacking AVX, AMX, and hyperthreading capabilities.

Benchmark data indicates a mix of average and weak performance profiles. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores are in the average tier, and single-threaded gzip compression demonstrates strong performance at 33.06 GB/sec. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the weak category. Memory performance is mixed, with large-block read-only bandwidth reaching an average tier of 45.94 GB/sec, while small-block reads and large-block writes are weak. Passmark CPU scores and database operations are weak to poor, and LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are poor for prompt processing and weak for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2ps_v6 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on an ARM architecture, which provides a lower-cost entry point for memory-intensive workloads compared to x86 alternatives. However, the trade-off is lower multi-threaded compute and database performance, as evidenced by weak Passmark database and Redis SET benchmarks. This server is recommended for memory-optimized workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing, such as lightweight caching, single-threaded text processing, or basic web serving.
